name: Constructivism

influenced_by: the 1917 Russian Revolution's call for art in service of industry and the state

garments: utilitarian worker's clothing, designed by some Constructivist artists (Varvara Stepanova) as a rejection of fashion for fashion's sake

media.title: El Lissitzky, Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge (1919)
Alexander Rodchenko's graphic design and photography (1920s)

reacts_against: art-for-art's-sake entirely, insisting that art should serve industrial production and the new Soviet state — hence its hard geometry, red-black-white posters and photomontage.

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Geometric abstraction, industrial materials (metal, glass, plastic), dynamic diagonal compositions, photomontage, sans-serif typography, structural forms
wiki_facts.key_colours: Limited palettes, often featuring bold red, black, and white
wiki_facts.related_aesthetics: BauhausCubismDeconstructivismDe StijlFuturismInternational Typographic StyleNeue Slowenische KunstSoviet ChicSuprematism
wiki_facts.key_values: Art in service of social revolution ("art into life"), rejection of "art for art's sake," utilitarianism, functionalism, collectivism, embrace of technology

findings: light — about 46% of the measured color is pale or near-white
mostly muted — about 85% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
